problem_statement: In the previous 18-agent run, Beta-1 was still processing while 5 other teams sat idle. No mechanism existed for idle teams to help busy teams, for teams to request assistance, for direct team-to-team coordination, or for dynamic work redistribution. This design addresses all of these gaps.

architecture_constraints.bus: JSONL append-only files, POSIX atomic writes < 4096 bytes, channels map to files
architecture_constraints.state: SQLite WAL mode, shared across all agents, retry-on-busy pattern

note_on_msg_types: The existing VALID_MSG_TYPES in bus.py must be extended. Alternatively, all new message subtypes can be encoded within the 'request'/'response'/'info' types using a body.subtype field to avoid modifying the bus core. We recommend the body.subtype approach for backward compatibility.

feature_1_team_help_protocol.title: Team Help Protocol
feature_1_team_help_protocol.description: Enables busy teams to request help and idle teams to offer assistance, with structured negotiation and work assignment.

body.description: Need help processing remaining 400 KB entries - parsing and indexing

work_units.output_spec: JSON array of parsed entries written to /path/to/output
JSON array of parsed entries written to /path/to/output

indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_work_units_request ON work_units(request_id);

help_offers.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS help_offers (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    offer_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES help_requests(request_id),
    offering_team TEXT NOT NULL,
    offering_agent TEXT NOT NULL,
    capabilities_matched TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON array
    can_handle_units TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON array of unit_ids

);
indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_help_offers_request ON help_offers(request_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_help_offers_status ON help_offers(status);

protocol_flow: 1. Busy team decomposes remaining work into divisible work_units, each with clear input/output
2. Busy team publishes help-request to 'topic-help' channel with all work_units listed
3. Busy team INSERTs help_request row and work_unit rows into SQLite
4. Idle teams polling 'topic-help' see the request
5. Idle team checks its own capabilities against required_capabilities
6. If match, idle team publishes help-offer referencing the request_id and listing which unit_ids it can handle
7. Idle team INSERTs help_offer row into SQLite
8. Requesting team (or coordinator) evaluates offers:
a. Checks capability match quality
b. Prefers teams with more available agents or faster start times
c. Assigns work_units to offering teams (may split across multiple offers)
9. Requesting team publishes help-accept with assigned unit_ids and a direct_channel name
10. Requesting team UPDATEs work_unit rows: assigned_to_team, status='assigned', assigned_at
11. Offering team receives accept, begins work on assigned units
12. Offering team establishes direct channel for ongoing coordination (see Feature 3)
13. On completion of each unit, offering team publishes work-complete to 'topic-help'
14. Offering team UPDATEs work_unit: status='completed', output_location, completed_at
15. Requesting team UPDATEs help_request: completed_units++, status='fulfilled' when all done
bus_cli_extensions: help-status [--request_id <id>]  -- show status of all help requests or a specific one
help-list [--status open|fulfilled|cancelled]  -- list help requests by status

feature_2_idle_detection_auto_reassignme.description: The coordinator detects idle teams after phase completion and proactively redistributes remaining work from busy teams.

body.target_team: string (team that should split its work)

splittable_units: array of work_unit objects that can be reassigned
body.unsplittable_reason: string (if work cannot be split, explain why)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_status (

    current_phase TEXT,

indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_team_status_status ON team_status(status);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS redistributions (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    redistribution_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    from_team TEXT NOT NULL,

protocol_flow: 1. Team completes its assigned phase/work
2. Team publishes phase-complete-available to global channel with capabilities and agent count
3. Team UPDATEs team_status: status='idle', idle_since=now(), available_agents=N
4. Coordinator polls team_status table periodically (every heartbeat cycle, 30s)
5. Coordinator detects: idle teams exist AND active teams exist with remaining work
6. Coordinator queries active teams' progress (from team_progress table, see Feature 4)
7. Coordinator identifies the team with the most remaining work (highest ETA)
8. Coordinator publishes work-split-request to 'topic-coordination' targeting that team
9. Busy team receives request, decomposes its remaining work into splittable units
10. Busy team publishes work-split-response listing available units
11. Coordinator matches idle team capabilities to splittable units
12. Coordinator publishes work-redistribution assigning units to idle team
13. Coordinator INSERTs redistribution record in SQLite
14. Coordinator UPDATEs team_status: idle team status='helping'
15. Both teams establish direct channel (Feature 3) for coordination
16. Helping team works on assigned units, reports completion via Feature 1 protocol
17. On all-units-complete, coordinator UPDATEs redistribution: status='completed'

coordinator_auto_reassignment_algorithm.description: Runs in coordinator heartbeat loop after check_agents()
pseudocode: idle_teams = SELECT * FROM team_status WHERE status = 'idle' ORDER BY idle_since ASC
active_teams = SELECT * FROM team_status WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY last_progress_update ASC
# Find busiest active team with splittable work
for active_team in active_teams (sorted by remaining work DESC):

feature_3_direct_team_channels.title: Direct Team-to-Team Channels
feature_3_direct_team_channels.description: Enables any two teams to establish a private communication channel for direct coordination without going through the global bus.

rules: Team names are alphabetically sorted so the channel name is deterministic: direct-alpha-1-to-beta-1 (never direct-beta-1-to-alpha-1)
Both teams read and write to the same file
Channel names are registered in SQLite for discovery

body.ttl_minutes: number (how long the channel stays active, default 60)

active_channels: string array of channel names currently open

direct_channels.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS direct_channels (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    channel_name TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    team_a TEXT NOT NULL,
    team_b TEXT NOT NULL,
    purpose TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, active, closed
    initiated_by TEXT NOT NULL,

    accepted_at REAL,
    closed_at REAL,

team_presence.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_presence (
    team TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'available',  -- available, busy, helping, offline
    available_agents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    capabilities TEXT,  -- JSON array
    active_channels TEXT,  -- JSON array
    last_seen REAL NOT NULL
);

protocol_flow: 1. Team A wants to coordinate with Team B
2. Team A computes channel name: sort(['team-a', 'team-b']) -> 'direct-team-a-to-team-b'
3. Team A publishes channel-open to 'topic-channels' with purpose and TTL
4. Team A INSERTs direct_channels row: status='pending'
5. Team B polls 'topic-channels', sees the channel-open request
6. Team B publishes channel-accept to 'topic-channels'
7. Team B UPDATEs direct_channels: status='active', accepted_at=now()
8. Both teams now read/write to the direct channel JSONL file
9. Messages on the direct channel use standard bus format but with the direct channel name
10. Either team can close the channel by publishing channel-close to 'topic-channels'
11. On close, UPDATE direct_channels: status='closed', closed_at=now()
12. Expired channels (created_at + ttl_minutes * 60 < now) are auto-closed by coordinator cleanup
presence_protocol: 1. Each team broadcasts presence to 'topic-presence' every 60 seconds
2. Team UPSERTs team_presence row with current status, capabilities, and active channels
3. Any team can query team_presence table to discover available teams
4. Coordinator monitors presence for stale entries (last_seen > 120s) and marks them offline
bus_cli_extensions: who  -- list all teams with their current presence status

protocol_flow: 1. Each team sets up a progress reporting interval (every 60s) in its main loop
2. Team computes current progress: percent, ETA, bottleneck, work unit counts
3. Team publishes progress-update to 'topic-progress' channel
4. Team UPSERTs team_progress row in SQLite

6. Coordinator polls team_progress table every 120s

feature_5_capability_matching.title: Capability Matching
feature_5_capability_matching.description: Teams register their capabilities, and the system automatically matches idle teams with compatible help requests.

capability_taxonomy.description: Standardized capability identifiers. Teams register using these tags.

team_capabilities.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_capabilities (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    team TEXT NOT NULL,
    capability TEXT NOT NULL,
    proficiency INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
    registered_at REAL NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(team, capability)
);
indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_team_capabilities_cap ON team_capabilities(capability);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_team_capabilities_team ON team_capabilities(team);

matching_algorithm.description: Runs when a help-request arrives or when coordinator does auto-reassignment
pseudocode: # Find teams that have ALL required capabilities
candidates = SELECT DISTINCT team FROM team_capabilities
WHERE capability IN (required_caps) AND proficiency >= min_proficiency
GROUP BY team HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT capability) = len(required_caps)
team_caps = SELECT * FROM team_capabilities WHERE team = team
required_score = sum(proficiency for cap in required_caps) / len(required_caps)
preferred_count = count(cap in preferred_caps for cap in team_caps)
return sorted(candidates, key=lambda t: t.match_score, reverse=True)

protocol_flow: 1. At startup, each team registers capabilities to 'topic-capabilities' and INSERTs to team_capabilities
2. When a help-request arrives, coordinator (or requesting team) calls find_matching_teams()
3. Matching considers: all required capabilities present, proficiency level, preferred capabilities, team availability
4. Results are ranked by composite match_score
5. Top-matching idle team is auto-notified (or coordinator sends work-split to them)
6. Teams can update capabilities mid-session if they gain new ones (e.g., after receiving context from another team)
bus_cli_extensions: list-capabilities [--team <team>]  -- show capabilities for all or a specific team

feature_6_additional_productivity.title: Additional Productivity Features
feature_6_additional_productivity.description: Six additional features beyond the core five, designed to further optimize multi-team operations.

6a_work_stealing.title: Work Stealing (Proactive Help)
6a_work_stealing.description: Idle teams proactively scan for and claim unclaimed work units without waiting for explicit help requests. Unlike reactive help offers, work stealing is initiated entirely by the idle team.
6a_work_stealing.sqlite_additions: Uses existing work_units table. Add column: stealable INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1. Teams mark units as stealable=0 if they require sequential processing or shared context that cannot be transferred.
protocol_flow: 1. Idle team queries: SELECT * FROM work_units WHERE status='pending' AND stealable=1 ORDER BY estimated_minutes DESC
2. Idle team attempts to claim by publishing steal-claim and doing: UPDATE work_units SET assigned_to_team=? WHERE unit_id=? AND status='pending' (atomic CAS via BEGIN IMMEDIATE)
3. If UPDATE affected 1 row -> claim granted, publish steal-granted with granted=true
4. If UPDATE affected 0 rows -> unit already taken, try next one
5. Owner team is notified via the topic-work-stealing channel
6. Claiming team proceeds to work on the unit

6b_pipeline_chaining.title: Pipeline Chaining (Team A output -> Team B input)
6b_pipeline_chaining.description: Enables automatic handoff of outputs from one team as inputs to the next team in a processing pipeline. Reduces manual coordination overhead.

sqlite_table.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pipeline_stages (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    pipeline_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    pipeline_name TEXT,
    stage_order INTEGER NOT NULL,
    team TEXT NOT NULL,
    input_location TEXT,
    output_location TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, active, completed, failed
    started_at REAL,
    completed_at REAL,
    UNIQUE(pipeline_id, stage_order)
);

protocol_flow: 1. Coordinator (or lead team) defines pipeline with ordered stages
2. Pipeline definition published to 'topic-pipelines' and stored in pipeline_stages table
3. First stage team begins work
4. On completion, stage team publishes stage-complete with output_location
5. Coordinator detects completion, UPDATEs pipeline_stages, triggers next stage
6. Next-stage team receives notification with input_location pointing to previous output
7. Process repeats until all stages complete
8. If a stage fails, coordinator can reassign to another team with matching capabilities

6c_shared_scratchpad.title: Shared Scratchpad for Intermediate Results
6c_shared_scratchpad.description: A key-value store in SQLite where teams can publish intermediate findings, partial results, and shared context that other teams can query and build upon.

sqlite_table.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scratchpad (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON
    team TEXT NOT NULL,
    agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    category TEXT,  -- e.g. 'intermediate-result', 'shared-context', 'reference-data'
    ttl_seconds INTEGER DEFAULT 3600,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL,
    updated_at REAL NOT NULL
);
indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scratchpad_category ON scratchpad(category);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_scratchpad_team ON scratchpad(team);

protocol_flow: 1. Team writes intermediate result: INSERT INTO scratchpad (key, value, team, ...) with UPSERT
2. Other teams query by key or category: SELECT * FROM scratchpad WHERE key = ? OR category = ?
3. Values are JSON so any structured data can be shared
4. Expired entries (created_at + ttl_seconds < now) are cleaned by coordinator cleanup cycle
5. Teams can overwrite keys they own (UPSERT on key with team match)

6d_priority_escalation.title: Priority Escalation (Urgent Tasks Jump the Queue)
6d_priority_escalation.description: Allows teams or the coordinator to escalate task priority, preempting lower-priority work and triggering immediate reallocation.
6d_priority_escalation.sqlite_additions: Add priority column to work_units and help_requests tables. ALTER TABLE work_units ADD COLUMN priority TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium'; ALTER TABLE help_requests ADD COLUMN priority_override TEXT;
protocol_flow: 1. Agent or coordinator determines a task needs higher priority
2. Publishes priority-escalation to global channel
3. Updates priority in work_units or help_requests table
4. Coordinator checks: if escalated to 'critical', attempt to preempt lower-priority work
5. If a team is working on low-priority and a critical task is unassigned, coordinator sends work-split-request
6. Team pauses low-priority work, picks up critical task
7. Low-priority work goes back to work_units with status='pending'

6e_team_merge_split.title: Team Merging and Splitting Mid-Operation
6e_team_merge_split.description: Allows two small teams to merge into one larger team for a complex task, or a large team to split into two smaller teams for parallel work.
6e_team_merge_split.sqlite_additions: Add parent_team and merge_history columns to agents table. ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN parent_team TEXT; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS team_operations (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, operation_type TEXT NOT NULL, operation_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, details TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', created_at REAL NOT NULL, completed_at REAL);
protocol_flow_merge: 1. Coordinator or team lead determines two teams should merge
3. Both teams acknowledge on their channels
4. Agent records updated: UPDATE agents SET team = merged_team_name WHERE team IN (team_a, team_b)
5. New team inherits combined capabilities (union of both team_capabilities entries)
6. Old team channels closed, new team uses new channel names
protocol_flow_split: 1. Coordinator determines a team is too large for its current work
2. Publishes team-split request specifying agent assignments per new team
3. Agent records updated: UPDATE agents SET team = new_team WHERE agent_id IN (...)
4. Capabilities re-registered for each new sub-team
5. Each new sub-team receives its work assignment

6f_load_balancing.title: Continuous Load Balancing
6f_load_balancing.description: Coordinator continuously monitors work distribution across teams and proactively rebalances to prevent any single team from becoming a bottleneck.

mechanism.description: Uses progress data (Feature 4) and capability data (Feature 5) to compute load imbalance scores and trigger rebalancing.
mechanism.imbalance_threshold: If any team's ETA exceeds 2x the average ETA of active teams, trigger rebalancing

sqlite_table.create_statement:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS load_balance_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,  -- imbalance-detected, rebalance-triggered, rebalance-completed
    from_team TEXT,
    to_team TEXT,
    imbalance_ratio REAL,
    units_moved INTEGER,
    created_at REAL NOT NULL
);

protocol_flow: 1. Coordinator reads team_progress every heartbeat cycle (30s)
2. Computes average ETA across active teams
3. If any team ETA > 2x average, flag imbalance
4. Check cooldown: if last rebalance < 300s ago, skip
5. Identify up to 25% of slowest team's pending work_units that are stealable
6. Find best idle or least-loaded team with matching capabilities
7. Execute redistribution using Feature 2 protocol
8. Log event in load_balance_events table
9. Publish load-balance notification to global channel

phase_1_core.title: Core Coordination (implement first)
phase_1_core.rationale: Progress tracking, presence, and capability registration are prerequisites for the help protocol and auto-reassignment. They are also the simplest to implement.

phase_2_help_system.title: Help Request/Response System
phase_2_help_system.rationale: The core help system depends on progress data, presence, and capabilities. These two features are tightly coupled and should be implemented together.

phase_3_advanced.title: Advanced Productivity
phase_3_advanced.rationale: These build on the help system and add proactive optimization.

phase_4_optional.title: Optional Enhancements
phase_4_optional.rationale: These are nice-to-have features that add flexibility but are not required for basic multi-team coordination.

risks.risk: Message size limit (4096 bytes) may be too small for help requests with many work units
risks.mitigation: Store work unit details in SQLite, reference by ID in bus messages. Keep bus messages as notifications, SQLite as source of truth.

risks.risk: SQLite contention with 14 new tables and 18+ agents
risks.mitigation: WAL mode handles concurrent reads well. Writes are serialized but fast. Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for CAS operations (work stealing). Monitor busy_timeout errors.

risks.risk: Channel proliferation with direct channels between N teams could create O(N^2) JSONL files
risks.mitigation: With 6 teams max, this is at most 15 files. TTL-based auto-close prevents accumulation. EpochRotator handles cleanup.

risks.risk: Stale presence data if a team crashes without sending presence=offline
risks.mitigation: Coordinator detects stale presence (last_seen > 120s) via existing dead_agent detection. Auto-mark offline.
